SchemaGuardrail.enforce has two distinct phases: (1) json.loads() wrapped in a try/except that raises SchemaViolation, and (2) a loop over self.schema.items() that checks presence then type, coercing with expected_type(value) when needed — raise SchemaViolation if the coercion throws.

For coercion: if isinstance(value, expected_type) is already True, store it directly. Otherwise call expected_type(value) inside a try/except (ValueError, TypeError) and raise SchemaViolation on failure. Return only the keys present in self.schema — drop extras.

PIIRedactor.redact applies three regex substitutions in order: email (user@domain.tld → [EMAIL]), phone (\(?\d{3}\)?[\s.\-]?\d{3}[\s.\-]\d{4} → [PHONE]), card (\b\d{13,19}\b → [CARD]). Apply email first, then phone, then card — ordering prevents interference between patterns.
